national basketball team|National team]]}} }} '''Mark Ellsworth Madsen''' (born January 28, 1976) is an American [[basketball]] coach and former NBA player who is the head coach of the [[California Golden Bears men's basketball|California Golden Bears]] of the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]] (ACC). Due to his hustle and physical style of play, he received the nickname "Mad Dog" while playing for the San Ramon Valley High School Wolves, and the moniker continued during his time with the Stanford Cardinal and beyond. He played professionally in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]], winning two [[NBA championships]]. He also played for the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]]. ==College career== Madsen played [[National Collegiate Athletic Association|NCAA]] basketball at [[Stanford]], where he finished his career ranked in the school's career top 10 in blocks and rebounds. In addition, Madsen helped the Cardinal to four NCAA tournament appearances, including a [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship#Final Four|Final Four]] berth in 1998. Perhaps his signature moment at Stanford was his dunk and free throw that gave Stanford a lead over [[University of Rhode Island|Rhode Island]], propelling the team into the Final Four, where it lost to eventual champion Kentucky. Madsen was a two-time All-American and a two-time [[List of All-Pacific-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-10]] selection. ==Professional career== === Los Angeles Lakers (2000–2003) === The [[Los Angeles Lakers]] selected Madsen in the first round (29th pick overall) of the [[2000 NBA draft]].{{Cite web |title=2000 NBA Draft |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/draft/NBA_2000.html |access-date=2026-06-28 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}} He contributed to the Lakers' [[NBA Finals|NBA championships]] in 2001 and 2002, and became well known for his goofy dances at the victory parades for those championships. Talking about his prime with the Lakers, [[Shaquille O'Neal]] said that the only player who could thwart him from his dominant play was Madsen. "He used to beat me up in practice", O'Neal said.{{cite news|url=http://lakersblog.latimes.com/lakersblog/2011/11/shaq-shaquille-oneal-kobe-bryant-.html|title=Shaquille O'neal Kobe Bryant|website=lakersblog.latimes.com|access-date=2023-02-21|date=November 2011}} === Minnesota Timberwolves (2003–2009) === Madsen signed with the Timberwolves as a free agent on a two-year, minimum contract before the start of the [[2003–04 NBA season]]. He played six seasons for the Wolves, after re-signing on a five-year, $12.1 million deal following the [[2004–05 NBA season|2004–05 season]].{{Cite web |date=2003-07-28 |title=Monday roundup: Madsen leaves, Grant arrives |url=https://www.espn.ph/nba/story?id=1586603 |access-date=2024-02-20 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=Mark Madsen Career Stats - NBA |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/stats/_/id/496 |access-date=2024-02-20 |website=ESPN |language=en}} On July 20, 2009, Madsen was traded to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] along with [[Craig Smith (basketball, born 1983)|Craig Smith]] and [[Sebastian Telfair]] in exchange for [[Quentin Richardson]].{{Cite web| url=http://www.nba.com/clippers/news/breakingnews090720.html | title=Clippers Acquire Telfair, Smith and Madsen from Minnesota for Richardson | work=[[NBA.com]] | date=July 20, 2009 | access-date=July 21, 2009}} On August 21, 2009, he was waived by the Clippers.{{Cite web| url=http://www.nba.com/clippers/news/breakingnews090821.html | title=Clippers Waive Mark Madsen | work=[[NBA.com]] | date=August 21, 2009 | access-date=August 22, 2009}} Madsen's final NBA game was played on April 15, 2009, in a 90–97 loss to the Sacramento Kings. In his final game, Madsen was the team's starting power forward, but he played for only {{frac|9|1|2}} minutes and recorded no stats. His career averages were 2.2 points, 2.6 rebounds, and 0.4 assists in 11.8 minutes played per game. ==Coaching career== === Los Angeles D-Fenders (2013) === Following being waived, Madsen was hired as the assistant coach for the [[Utah Flash]] of the [[NBA G League|NBA Development League]] (D-League).{{Cite web|url=https://sltrib.com/|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150711135904/http://www.sltrib.com/sports/ci_14207919|url-status=dead|title=The Salt Lake Tribune - Utah News, Sports, Religion & Entertainment|archive-date=July 11, 2015|website=The Salt Lake Tribune|access-date=February 21, 2023}} In 2012, he was hired as an assistant coach at Stanford.{{Cite web|url=https://www.sfgate.com/collegesports/article/stanford-hires-mark-madsen-as-assistant-coach-3612240.php|title=Stanford hires Mark Madsen as assistant coach|first=Tom|last=FitzGerald|date=June 6, 2012|website=SFGATE|access-date=February 21, 2023}} On May 13, 2013, he was named head coach of the [[South Bay Lakers|Los Angeles D-Fenders]], a D-League team owned by the Los Angeles Lakers.{{Cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/losangeles/130513_madsen.html|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130601034257/http://www.nba.com/dleague/losangeles/130513_madsen.html|url-status=dead|title=Los Angeles D-Fenders Name Mark Madsen as Head Coach|website=[[NBA.com]] |archive-date=June 1, 2013|access-date=February 21, 2023}} === Los Angeles Lakers (2013-2019) === On July 19, 2013, Madsen was promoted to a player development coach position with the Lakers.{{cite news | url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=13834 | title=Lakers hire Mark Madsen as player development coach | work=InsideHoops.com | date=July 19, 2013 | access-date=July 19, 2013 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151123214450/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=13834 | archive-date=November 23, 2015 | url-status=dead }} On September 16, 2014, Madsen was promoted to full-fledged assistant coach by Byron Scott.{{Cite web|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/lakers/lakersnow/la-sp-ln-lakers-byron-scott-coaching-staff-20140916-story.html|title=Lakers announce Byron Scott's coaching staff - Los Angeles Times|last=Pincus|first=Eric|website=[[Los Angeles Times]]|date=September 16, 2014|access-date=October 7, 2018}} After Byron Scott was dismissed as head coach of the Lakers, new head coach Luke Walton retained Madsen as assistant coach on July 1, 2016.{{Cite news|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/160701assistant_coaches|title=Lakers Announce Assistant Coach Hires {{!}} Los Angeles Lakers|work=Los Angeles Lakers|access-date=October 7, 2018}} === Utah Valley (2019–2023) === Madsen was hired as the head coach at [[Utah Valley University]] on April 14, 2019.{{cite news|url=https://www.heraldextra.com/sports/college/uvu/basketball-men/lakers-assistant-coach-mark-madsen-to-be-introduced-monday-as/article_8a6bb491-2a3c-5956-95ee-2dbdd125ddaf.html|title=Lakers assistant coach Mark Madsen to be introduced Monday as new UVU men's basketball coach|access-date=May 28, 2019|date=April 14, 2019|language=en|author=Lloyd, Jared|periodical=Daily Herald}} === California (2023–present) === Madsen was hired as the head coach at the [[University of California, Berkeley]] on March 29, 2023. Madsen is the 19th men's basketball head coach in Cal history.{{cite web |title=Mark Madsen hired by Cal: Bears land Utah Valley coach who was a star player for rival Stanford |date=March 29, 2023 |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/mark-madsen-hired-by-cal-bears-land-utah-valley-coach-who-was-a-star-player-for-rival-stanford/}}{{cite web | last=Athletics | first=California Golden Bears | title=Mark Madsen Named Cal Men's Basketball Head Coach | website=California Golden Bears Athletics | date=2023-03-29 | url=https://calbears.com/news/2023/3/29/mens-basketball-mark-madsen-named-cal-mens-basketball-head-coach.aspx | access-date=2024-10-16}} On March 12, 2024, Madsen signed a two-year contract extension through the 2029–30 season.{{cite web |url=https://calbears.com/news/2024/3/12/mens-basketball-mark-madsen-signs-contract-extension.aspx |title=Mark Madsen Signs Contract Extension |date=March 12, 2024 |publisher=Cal Athletics}} His salary for the 2025-2026 season is $2.8 million. ==Personal life == Madsen is a member of [[the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints]]. Madsen speaks Spanish, acquiring the language from a two-year [[Missionary (LDS Church)|mission]] abroad in [[Málaga, Spain]] on behalf of his church following his graduation from high school. As a youth, Madsen attained the rank of [[Eagle Scout (Boy Scouts of America)|Eagle Scout]] and credits Scouting with teaching him about leadership, character and mentoring.{{cite book | last = Townley | first = Alvin | url = http://www.thomasdunnebooks.com/TD_TitleDetail.aspx?ISBN=0312366531 | title = Legacy of Honor: The Values and Influence of America's Eagle Scouts | year = 2007 | publisher = St. Martin's Press | location = New York | pages = 205–206 | isbn = 978-0-312-36653-7 | access-date = December 29, 2006 | archive-date = September 24, 2008 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20080924165201/http://www.thomasdunnebooks.com/TD_TitleDetail.aspx?ISBN=0312366531 | url-status = dead }} In fall 2010, Madsen enrolled in the [[Stanford Graduate School of Business]]. In June 2012, he received an [[Master of Business Administration|M.B.A.]] degree with a Certificate in Public Management.{{cite web | url=http://www.gsb.stanford.edu/commencement/awards.html | title=Certificate and Award Recipients | publisher=Stanford Graduate School of Business | access-date=July 1, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120930004641/http://www.gsb.stanford.edu/commencement/awards.html|archive-date=September 30, 2012}} Madsen married Hannah Harkness on September 3, 2016. The Madsens have three boys and two daughters.{{Cite web |date=2024-11-05 |title=Cal's First Victory Comes Before Coach Mark Madsen's Fifth Child |url=https://www.si.com/college/cal/basketball/cal-s-first-victory-comes-before-coach-mark-madsen-s-fifth-child-01jbyk052p2j |access-date=2025-01-05 |website=California Golden Bears On SI |language=en-US}} ==NBA career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend|champion=y}} ===Regular season=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="background:#afe6ba;" align="left" | {{nbay|2000}}† | align="left" | [[2000–01 Los Angeles Lakers season|L.A.
